tagline: Glacier-made hills from Fort Leavenworth to the Nebraska line.
intro: From K-92 by the gates of Fort Leavenworth, K-7 heads north over rolling hills and rock-strewn valleys to Atchison on the Missouri, and on to Troy. Outside Troy the byway leaves the highway for a run of county road, 180th Road, Last Chance Road and 195th Road, then rejoins K-7 for White Cloud and the Nebraska line, about 63 miles in all.
Ancient glaciers shaped this ground, and wind and rain have worked on it since. The towns came in the 1850s, with the steamboats on the river and the wagon road west out of St. Joseph.

moments.title: Atchison
moments.text: A Missouri River town founded in 1854, the first eastern terminus of the Santa Fe railway, and home to the Amelia Earhart Birthplace Museum.

moments.title: Troy
moments.text: The Doniphan County seat grew from a stop on the wagon road to Oregon and California, where Richard Burton, passing in 1860, saw only "a few wretched shanties called Troy".

moments.title: White Cloud
moments.text: Seat of the Iowa Tribe's government, where an obelisk honors a ten-year-old who in 1913 raised a pig, sold it for $25 and gave the money to a mission to lepers.
